findings.reason: PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.RunTask only calls Directory.CreateDirectory and writes a file when ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns true. It never deletes anything. The UpdateItems target swaps in a file whenever Exists('$(IntermediateOutputPath)prelink/%(Filename)%(Extension)') is true. So if a library that once needed the rewrite is upgraded to a version that doesn't, the old prelink copy is still swapped in before ILLink.
findings.claim: Old copies in obj/prelink are never deleted, and the swap uses any file there that matches by filename, so an upgraded library can be silently replaced by an old rewritten copy.
findings.evidence: `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems` swaps every ResolvedFileToPublish .dll for which `Exists('$(IntermediateOutputPath)prelink/%(Filename)%(Extension)')` is true. It does not use the task's `ModifiedAssemblies` output. PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.RunTask only calls `Directory.CreateDirectory (OutputDirectory)` and writes a file when `ProcessAssemblyDesigner` returns true; it never removes old files. Trigger: publish with library A v1, which has a legacy Resource designer, so prelink/A.dll is written. Upgrade A to v2, which uses the designer assembly or has no legacy designer. The task reruns (or is skipped), `FindResourceDesigner` returns false so nothing is written, and the old prelink/A.dll still exists. The Exists() swap then replaces v2 with the rewritten v1 before ILLink.

members.claim: The swap uses any file that happens to be in `obj/.../prelink/` and nothing ever deletes old copies, so after a library upgrade the app can silently ship an old rewritten copy of that library in place of the current one.

members.claim: Stale prelink assemblies can replace updated dependencies, causing builds to ship obsolete code.
members.evidence: After a legacy library has produced prelink/Library.dll, replace it with a version that uses the modern designer or no longer has a resource designer. PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.RunTask writes a copy only when ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns true and never deletes previous copies. Even when the task reruns, this target substitutes any existing prelink file based solely on its filename, so the old Library.dll replaces the updated dependency.

findings.reason: Outputs is only the stamp file, and FileWrites for the prelink copies is added only when the target actually runs. The diff also removes the old fallbacks: the post-trim FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep in PostTrimmingPipeline.cs and the TrimmerRootDescriptor in Resource.Designer.targets. So if the prelink copies are missing, nothing rewrites the library. I kept it at medium because the trigger needs the prelink folder cleaned while the stamp survives, or a new input whose timestamp is older than the stamp.
findings.claim: The up-to-date check only looks at a stamp file, so missing prelink copies are not regenerated, and the original legacy-designer library goes to ILLink without the rewrite.
findings.evidence: `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` has `Outputs="$(_AndroidStampDirectory)_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.stamp"`, and its `<FileWrites Include="@(_PreTrimmingModifiedAssembly)" />` is added only when the target actually runs. If prelink/*.dll is removed (manual clean of obj/prelink, or possibly IncrementalClean on a build where the target was skipped and FileWrites lacked them), the stamp is still newer than the inputs, the task is skipped, Exists() is false, and the original library passes to ILLink. The old post-trim rewrite (removed from PostTrimmingPipeline.cs) and the TrimmerRootDescriptor (removed from Resource.Designer.targets) no longer back this up. Before this change the rewrite ran on every build because `_PostTrimmingPipeline` has no Inputs/Outputs. The same stamp check also skips the task when a newly added input .dll has an older timestamp than the stamp.
